taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest's "six days from Saturday, Oct 24" lands on Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

- On Oct 30, 2026, the US is still in Daylight Time (PDT, UTC−7), since DST ends Nov 1, 2026.
- Spain's DST ends earlier, on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so by Oct 30, Madrid is on standard time (CET, UTC+1).

Convert: 23:59 PDT (UTC−7) on Oct 30 → add 7 hours → 06:59 UTC on Oct 31 → add 1 hour (CET) → 07:59 on Oct 31 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Today (Friday) is Oct 30, 2026, so "this coming Monday" is **November 2, 2026**.

- Los Angeles: By Nov 2, DST has ended (ended Nov 1, 2026), so LA is on PST = UTC−8.
- Madrid: DST ended Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

Difference: UTC+1 − (UTC−8) = 9 hours ahead of LA.

10:00 AM PST + 9 hours = 7:00 PM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) until the clocks go back on the last Sunday of October — Sunday, October 25, 2026 at 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET (i.e., 01:00 UTC).

Start of hackathon: Saturday, Oct 24, 2026, 18:00 CEST = 16:00 UTC.

Adding exactly 48 real hours: 16:00 UTC + 48h = Monday, Oct 26, 2026, 16:00 UTC.

Since the clock change already happened before this point, Madrid is now on CET (UTC+1):
16:00 UTC + 1h = 17:00 CET.

So the hackathon ends at 17:00 local time on Monday, October 26, 2026 (one hour earlier than a naive +48h calculation would suggest, because of the fall-back DST transition).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The start time is Oct 26, 2026, 10:00 AM PT. Since DST in the US ends Nov 1, 2026, this is still PDT (UTC−7), so start = 17:00 UTC.

72 hours later = Oct 29, 2026, 17:00 UTC.

Madrid (CET/CEST) switches back to standard time on the last Sunday of October 2026, which is Oct 25, 2026. So by Oct 29, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

17:00 UTC + 1 hour = 18:00 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to work through the timezone conversions and DST rules carefully.

**Step 1: Determine ET offset on October 31, 2026**
DST ends in the US on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's November 1. So October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM is still in EDT (UTC−4).

**Step 2: Convert submission close time to UTC**
Oct 31, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT (UTC−4) → add 4 hours → Nov 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC.

**Step 3: Add 36 hours**
Nov 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = Nov 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC.

**Step 4: Determine Madrid's offset on November 2, 2026**
DST ends in the EU on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So by November 2, 2026, Madrid is back on CET (UTC+1).

**Step 5: Convert to Madrid time**
Nov 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = Nov 2, 2026, 16:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Converting the Unix timestamp**

1. Unix timestamp: 1791788340 seconds since 1970‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC.
2. Using the known reference point 1609459200 = 2021‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC:
   1791788340 − 1609459200 = 182,329,140 seconds elapsed since then.
3. 182,329,140 s ÷ 86400 s/day = 2110 days, remainder 25,140 s.
4. 25,140 s = 6 h 59 m 00 s.
5. Adding 2110 days to 2021‑01‑01 (accounting for leap year 2024) lands on **2026‑10‑12**.
6. So the UTC timestamp is **2026‑10‑12 06:59:00 UTC**.

**Convert to Tokyo time (JST = UTC+9, no DST)**

06:59 UTC + 9 h = 15:59 JST, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid observes CEST (UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 25. The clocks shift back at 01:00 UTC (03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET) that day. Since the deadline (02:30 UTC) falls after this transition, Madrid is already on CET (UTC+1).

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Find the last Sunday of October 2026**
October 1, 2026 is a Thursday, so the Sundays in October are the 4th, 11th, 18th, and 25th → the last Sunday is **October 25, 2026**.

**Step 2 — Determine the Pacific Time offset**
In October, the U.S. is still on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC‑7). DST doesn't end until early November, so 11:59 PM Oct 25, 2026 PDT = UTC‑7.

**Step 3 — Convert to UTC**
11:59 PM PDT Oct 25 + 7 hours = **06:59 UTC, Oct 26, 2026**.

**Step 4 — Convert to Madrid time**
Spain (CET/CEST) also ends DST on the last Sunday of October — which is also Oct 25, 2026, at 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET (i.e., 01:00 UTC).
Since our UTC moment (06:59 UTC, Oct 26) is after that transition, Madrid is already on **CET (UTC+1)**.

So: 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = **07:59 on October 26, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

DST in the US ends on the first Sunday of November — in 2026, that's **November 1, 2026**. The clocks fall back from EDT to EST at 2:00 AM that day, so by 12:00 noon, Eastern Time is already in **EST (UTC-5)**.

Lima, Peru uses **UTC-5 year-round** (no DST), which is the same offset as EST.

So 12:00 noon EST on November 1, 2026 corresponds directly to 12:00 noon in Lima — no time difference to adjust for.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12. "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is equivalent to January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12, which is January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.

Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9, so add 9 hours: January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is in AEDT (UTC+11) on October 5, 2026 (DST starts Oct 4). New York is in EDT (UTC-4) at that time (DST ends Nov 1, 2026). The difference is 15 hours (New York behind Sydney).

5:00 PM Oct 5 Sydney → 6:00 AM UTC Oct 5 → 2:00 AM EDT Oct 5 in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
